title: The Mag Wrap 2025
subtitle: A motion system for The Mag Wrap
overview: This is where I got to play with 3D, motion and the slightly chaotic energy of a rap show.
I built an intro, loops and reusable graphics that could feel like one world without repeating the same shot.

hero.alt: The Mag Wrap 2025 — A motion system for The Mag Wrap

caption: The Mag Wrap 2025 · Main motion package

approach.label: Brief / Why I did it
paragraphs: I wanted to see how far I could push one visual idea across a whole motion package. Something loud and recognisable, with enough room to keep trying things.

approach.label: Process / Tools & thinking process
paragraphs: I used Blender and Houdini for the 3D work, Nuke and After Effects for compositing and motion, and DaVinci Resolve to bring it together.
I started with a few shapes, materials and movements, then treated them as a kit. The question was always: can this idea work as an intro, a loop and a small on-screen graphic?

outcome.label: My role / What I made
paragraphs: I worked on the art direction, 3D animation and motion design: the intro, show IDs, looping backgrounds and reusable graphics. A mix of making individual shots and figuring out how the pieces should fit together.

outcome.label: Result / What I learned
paragraphs: The useful part was learning to build a system that still left room to play. Reusing the same visual ingredients made the package more coherent, and gave me more time to spend on the moments that needed something different.

title: Barbour

overview: Monopo London invited me to direct CGI and VFX for Barbour’s Icons in Quilting campaign.
The iconic quilt spreads across London, New York, Shanghai and Seoul, followed by a trail of British countryside.

approach.label: Brief
paragraphs: Translate Barbour's Icons in Quilting platform into scroll-stopping fake out-of-home films for London, New York, Seoul, and Shanghai while carrying the British countryside into each city.

approach.label: Process
paragraphs: I directed the CGI production, reconstructing and tracking live-action city plates, animating the signature quilt, and building procedural nature trails in Blender and Houdini before compositing each scene for a convincing mixed-reality finish.

outcome.label: My role

title: Chainer
subtitle: Small objects, strange worlds
overview: I used jewellery as a starting point for a series of 3D worlds. Small objects, strange landscapes, and a lot of playing with light and materials.
The experiment grew into animation, sound and a website. I wanted all of it to feel like it belonged to the same place.
caption: Chainer · Product visualization film

approach.label: Brief / Why I did it
paragraphs: I wanted to make jewellery feel interesting before you even looked at the product details. It was a chance to build a world around a small object and see how much atmosphere I could get out of it.

approach.label: Process / Tools & thinking process
paragraphs: My toolkit was 3D modelling, materials, lighting and animation, alongside sound design and web development.

I started with the object and its material, then built a setting around it. I kept looking for a balance: enough of a world to make the image interesting, but not so much that the jewellery disappeared.

outcome.label: My role / What I made
paragraphs: I shaped the art direction, animated the product scenes, worked on the sound and carried the visual direction into the website. The fun part was connecting the still images, moving shots and interactions.

outcome.label: Result / What I learned
paragraphs: A strong image does not need a complicated scene. A clear silhouette, a useful reflection and one good contrast can do a lot. Taking the same ideas into motion and the website also made me pay more attention to how the pieces connect.

title: Shelby
subtitle: Custom Device & Merch Mockups
overview: Ashfall Studio asked me to create custom mockups for their Shelby brand case study. Shelby is a decentralized storage platform, and Ashfall developed its brand identity and motion system.
I brought the identity into a set of 3D scenes, from MacBook and iPad mockups to branded pins, event badges, bottles and clothing.

hero.alt: Shelby website on a MacBook in a sunlit workspace with wood surfaces and a perforated wall

caption: Shelby · Custom MacBook mockup

approach.label: Brief
paragraphs: Create custom mockups for Ashfall’s presentation of the Shelby identity. The set needed to show the brand on screens and physical objects, with room for both the website’s motion and the details of the merchandise.

approach.label: Process
paragraphs: I placed the devices in a warm workspace, using wood, a perforated backdrop and directional sunlight to frame the screens. For the merch, I used simple colour fields and close views so the materials, shapes and printed graphics could lead.

outcome.label: My role
paragraphs: I created the custom 3D device and merch mockups for the case study. I worked with Martin Ehrlich, Ashfall’s founder, on creative direction and with motion designer Dominik Budimir to bring Ashfall’s identity into these scenes.

outcome.label: Result
paragraphs: The finished set presents Shelby across digital and physical applications: a website on devices, a rotating pin, an event badge, a bottle and clothing. Together, the scenes give Ashfall a range of still and animated views for their brand case study.

title: Trezor
subtitle: Hardware Wallet Product Animation
overview: I worked with Yiskra to create dynamic product animations for Trezor’s online store. The brief was to match Trezor’s aesthetic while showing the hardware wallet through realistic lighting and intricate motion.
The animations bring out the shape, surface details and colour of the product, keeping the wallet at the centre of each shot.

hero.alt: Green Trezor hardware wallet rotating against a light background

caption: Trezor · Product animation

approach.label: Brief
paragraphs: Create dynamic animations for Trezor’s product page in the store. The visuals needed to fit the brand’s aesthetic and show the hardware wallet clearly across three colours.

approach.label: Process
paragraphs: I paired intricate rotations with controlled lighting to reveal the wallet’s profile, screen and textured back. Reflections help describe the surfaces, while the light background keeps attention on the product.

outcome.label: My role
paragraphs: I handled the 3D work, motion and lighting. Tomas Gnosis Snop managed the project at Yiskra.

outcome.label: Result
paragraphs: A set of product animations in black, green and orange, with a consistent approach to lighting and motion across the three versions. The close views show the wallet’s surface details, while the wider sequence follows its shape through a gradual rotation.
